correctness.rationale: For m=N/2 and odds u=q/(1-q), at fixed switch count and first sign the two ordered run lists are independent uniform positive compositions of m. Their counts give the stated odd/even weights. In the Bessel comparison, writing a=j-1 and x=mu, the relative clipped-product deficits in the odd and even summands are bounded by a(a+1)/m and (a+1)^2/m, respectively. Summed against the two Bessel series, their combined bound is x(x+1)/m times I_0(2x)+I_1(2x), before the common 2x factor. Thus the relative error vanishes uniformly for odds tilted by s in a compact interval around 1. The resulting log conditional PGF is 2x(s-1)+(log s)/2+o(1), with 2x=T+o(1). Chernoff tilts s=exp(±c/log^2 T) give |K-T|<=T/log^2 T with probability tending to one since T/log^4 T diverges. For a color with r parts, discretizing r-1 iid cuts by ceil((m-1)U) moves each cut by at most one in m-scale. Conditional on distinct cuts the sorted set is uniform; resampling a uniform set only on collision gives an exact composition coupling, and the collision probability is O(r^2/m). Uniformly over concentrated switch counts, the largest error when replacing all (K/N)-scaled parts by iid exponentials is o_P(1): the cut error is O(K/N), and the sample-mean error times the largest exponential is O_P(log r/sqrt(r)), with K/(2r)=1+O(1/K). Independent exponential arrays give the product Laplace functional; log(r/K) tends to -log 2. The normalization transfer to T has uniform maximum displacement o_P(1) by the sharper switch concentration. Compact-window counts of the coupled exponentials are tight, so this displacement does not change the Laplace limit. Their maxima centered by log r are tight from the explicit exponential maximum law. That last fact, and the absence of limit atoms at z, justify the unbounded upper-tail counts and the longest-run law beyond vague convergence alone.
residual_risks: The packaged 285 checks, including floating-point Bessel diagnostics, were not rerun and do not prove the point-process limit. The proof is only for symmetric switching, exact balance, and the stated T regime.

value.rationale: Exact balance strongly constrains the lengths and couples the run colors through the random number of switches. Showing that the colors nevertheless separate in the upper-tail limit answers more than the usual longest-run question, and applies on the independently motivated crossover scale. The full PPP identifies the joint law of counts in multiple extreme windows, not just the Gumbel marginal.
residual_risks: No claim of finite-sample independence, quantitative PPP approximation, or validity at fixed q.
